In a recent article in the Sunday Express, the writer expressed confidence that Britain's young athletes will soon be amongst the world's best. Amongst those mentioned, we were favoured by the mention of seven members:—Broadbent, Clay, Frost, Brown, Marchant, Burfitt and Main.
We were unable to see much of Stan this summer and we hope that next summer we shall see him in action against Clay and Frost. Len Marchant has been running well in R.A.F. teams.

Jack Frost beat Reynolds of the Police in the 100 Yards with Stan Botwright third. The latter, however, won the 220 with Ted Read in second place.
Higgins, the Public Schools' quarter champion, beat Ted Read in the 220, and scored a double by also winning the 440, in which Jack Frost finished third.
However, our team was sadly weakened by the absence of Marchant and Frost, who were on R.A.F. duties, and the terrific queue at Paddington looked like ending our journey before we had started.
